text:
jules: Quick sync — RFC followup idea: move service auth to a "claims-first" token shape where tokens carry minimal intent claims (svc_id, tenant_id, capability-set) and we keep policy evaluation outside the token. Thinking this buys clearer runtime routing + simpler exchange logic. Thoughts?
remy: Curious — does "claims-first" mean we stop encoding project/org hierarchy in the token name and instead rely on tenant_id claim?
sophia: Exactly. Instead of org:project:key prefixes we carry explicit claims and a stable claim schema version. That avoids brittle string parsing and makes delegation explicit.
jules: Right. Tradeoffs: runtime needs to enforce claim->role mapping (RBAC) and we add a short lookup step. But we get predictable token semantics and easier cross-tenant delegation patterns.
kai: Concern: extra lookups per request = perf hit. Our hot paths need <10ms p50 auth. How do we avoid adding latency?
sophia: We can cache claim->role mappings in the authn sidecar with LRU and TTL tuned to rollout cadence. Also keep a small on-disk snapshot per node for cold restarts.
maria: Also consider precomputed capability tokens for high-throughput internal calls (like backend-ingest). Those would be minted with narrower TTL and skip some remote calls.
remy: What about migration from current API-key format? We still have tons of keys named org:svc:legacy.* and users will expect no breakage.
jules: Plan A (nonbreaking): introduce v2 tokens alongside v1, runtime accepts both. New services publish using v2. We add a transparent shim that extracts claims from v1 fallback when possible.
kai: Shim logic needs to be auditable. Otherwise we risk surprising mappings. Can we log shim mappings to telemetry with sampling?
sophia: Yes — log 1% of shim mappings with hashed original key + resolved claims + route. That gives signal without PII.
devops-bot: deploy-bot: Auth service can add /token/exchange endpoint for v1->v2 migration. Will run canary in us-west-2.
maria: One more: RBAC model — do we keep role IDs or shift to capability sets (capabilities are explicit verbs + resource types)?
jules: I prefer capability sets for fine-grained control and easier policy reasoning. Roles can be derived sets for UX.
remy: How do we represent inherited permissions (org -> project)? Claims-first could include an "ancestors" list but that makes tokens big.
sophia: Instead include a tenant_id and a scope field ("org" or "project") plus an optional assertion_id that points to a signed, short-lived delegation proof stored in the auth service. Runtime can fetch proof only when scope mismatch detected.
kai: That reduces token size and keeps common-case fast. Good.
maria: We should also define TTL policy: short for cross-tenant/delegation, medium for service-to-service, longer for operator keys — with enforced rotation.
jules: Agreed. Action items: 1) sophia + kai to prototype LRU cache + snapshot and measure added tail latency (due EOD Fri). 2) remy + maria to draft migration playbook and shim audit logging spec (PR next Tue). 3) I'll write a compact claim schema doc and v2 token shape.
sophia: I'll start a design doc and include sample token JSON + example exchange flow. Snippet for RFC:```json
{
  "iss": "redwood-auth",
  "sub": "svc:ingest-processor",
  "claims_version": "2",
  "tenant_id": "t-12345",
  "scope": "project",
  "capabilities": ["write:ingest","read:config"],
  "exp": 1717263599
}
```
remy: LGTM. One more nit: ensure our SDKs can surface the shim warning when v1 tokens used so customers see migration nudges.
jules: Good call. We'll add a non-erring telemetry header for SDKs to show in dashboards.
kai: If prototype numbers are bad, we can consider coalescing claim checks into the request router (batching lookups per batch). But let's measure first.
maria: Thanks — syncing offline to slot a quick architecture review next week. :thumbsup:
